new_issues.title: SignalEvent raises AttributeError instead of InvalidSignalError when Timestamp.meaning is not a TimeMeaning.
new_issues.why: Timestamp.__post_init__ validates only ns, so Timestamp(100, 'available_at') constructs. SignalEvent's identity check at signals.py:76 then fails and the message formats self.time.meaning.value, which raises AttributeError on a str/int/None. Slice 105 says a time whose meaning is not AVAILABLE_AT raises InvalidSignalError, and the same constructor already guards malformed time and time.ns types; this is the same raw-exception-instead-of-typed-error class the project fixed elsewhere (teccae5e). Still present at repo HEAD. hy4/1/1 asks for the regression test for this same crash.

new_issues.title: as_integer converts a non-Integral Real to float before the integrality check, so a high-precision Fraction rounds to an integer and is accepted.
new_issues.why: True: as_integer calls as_real (float(value)) then is_integer(), so Fraction(2**53+1, 2**53) becomes 1.0 and returns 1. Only a non-float Real with more than 53 bits of precision triggers it (Fraction, longdouble); parameter values come from floats/ints in practice. The fix commit for the case's bug kept 'other reals take the nearest float' as deliberate policy. Not the known B1, which is as_real on large Integrals.

new_issues.title: Element-loop guard is copied into test_labels.py and test_confidence.py with a node set that differs from test_import_boundary.py (GeneratorExp excluded).
new_issues.why: True: test_import_boundary.py ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES includes ast.GeneratorExp, the two new local copies exclude it. Test-code duplication and inconsistent policy, no production behavior affected; the fix commit 6078e2b consolidated it.

new_issues.title: LabelVocabulary.category_ids is annotated frozenset[int] but the runtime accepts set, needing pyright ignores.
new_issues.why: True: the annotation is frozenset[int] while __post_init__ accepts set or frozenset with a reportUnnecessaryIsInstance suppression, and tests pass sets with ignores. Typing/API-shape inconsistency; behavior is correct.

new_issues.title: _coerce has no default branch, so a future ParameterType member would silently return None.
new_issues.why: True for a hypothetical new enum member; today the match covers both members of ParameterType. Future-proofing (assert_never), no current defect.

new_issues.title: test_match_selects_the_branch_for_each_form runs a match in the test body and exercises no library code.
new_issues.why: True: the test matches on its own parametrized inputs and asserts a string it built; it only proves dataclass __match_args__. Low-value test, no production defect.

new_issues.title: No test pins SignalSequence ordering at the int64 extremes.
new_issues.why: True: _require_time_order compares neighbours correctly; no test covers INT64_MAX followed by INT64_MIN. Missing test for an already-correct path (added later in 6078e2b).

new_issues.title: test_confidence.py helpers _array and _mask are annotated with bare np.ndarray.
new_issues.why: The bare annotations are real and looser than the sibling NDArray[...] helpers. sonnet-high's claim that strict pyright fails is wrong: pyright at head (strict, tests included) reports 0 errors on test_confidence.py, as numpy 2 ndarray has defaulted type parameters. Style only.

new_issues.title: Test lines with trailing pyright-ignore comments exceed 88 chars and fail ruff E501 / format check in CI.
new_issues.why: Ran the repo's ruff on the head tree with its pyproject: 'ruff check' reports all checks passed and 'ruff format --check' reports all files formatted. E501 does not flag these lines, so CI does not fail.
